# We're an Agency, Not Just a Studio — Here's What That Actually Means for Your Quote

Quick Answer

Backyard Studio operates as a full-service agency across the UAE - Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain - which means every quote reflects creative strategy, account management, and revisions built in, not just a day rate for showing up with a camera. Typical projects range from AED 5,000 to AED 60,000+ depending on scope, and every quote is itemised so it's clear exactly what's included, not just a single number.

---

The Pattern That's Genuinely Hard on a Small Agency

It usually goes the same way. A potential client reaches out, and the conversation is thorough - genuinely thorough. Every project in the portfolio gets asked about. How was that lit? What was the story behind that edit? What's the process for revisions? How do you handle a brief that changes halfway through? Good questions, taken seriously, answered properly, often over calls that run well past the scheduled time.

Then the quote goes out. And sometimes, that's it. No reply, no "this is too much," no "we're going with someone else," just silence.

It's not that the questions weren't genuine in the moment. It's that reviewing a portfolio costs the client nothing, and it doesn't always occur to people that answering all of it properly costs the agency real time - time that could have gone into an actual paying project. When that happens repeatedly, it stops being a one-off and starts being a pattern worth being honest about.

---

Why This Happens More With an Agency Than a Solo Studio

A single freelance videographer's quote is usually simple: hours × rate, plus equipment. There's less to ask about, because there's less happening behind the number.

An agency quote is different, because an agency isn't selling hours with a camera - it's selling a full process: creative direction, a team of specialists, a structured revision process, and someone managing the project so nothing falls through the cracks. That's naturally more to ask about, and naturally invites more conversation before a decision. Most of the time, that conversation is worth having. The problem isn't the questions - it's when the questions replace an actual decision, one way or the other.

---

What's Actually Behind an Agency Quote (Not Just "Filming")

- **Creative strategy** — time spent understanding the actual goal behind the video, not just the format requested - **A specialist team** — director, cinematographer, editor, colourist, and sound designer, coordinated as one process - **Project management** — someone making sure the shoot, edit, and revisions stay on schedule - **Structured revisions** — built into the process, not billed as a surprise afterward - **Accountability** — one point of contact responsible for the outcome, not a loose collection of freelancers

A studio day rate can look cheaper on paper because it often doesn't include most of this. That's a fair trade-off for some projects. It's just not the same thing being compared.

These figures reflect Backyard Studio's actual published packages - every quote is itemised, so you can see exactly which parts of the process the number covers.

- **If the budget doesn't match, just say so** — "this is more than we expected" is a completely fine reply, and often leads to a scaled-down option that does fit - **Ask about scope alongside price** — "what does this number actually include" is more useful than the number alone - **A quote is a starting point, not a final offer** — Backyard Studio can usually adjust scope to fit a range, but only if that conversation happens - **Silence helps no one** — even a quick "not right now" lets both sides move on cleanly, rather than leaving a proposal open indefinitely

# How to Plan Your Video Shoot in Dubai: A Simple 4-Step Guide

Quick Answer

Planning a video shoot in Dubai comes down to four things: choosing the right location and confirming any filming permits it needs, deciding the look and styling for whoever's on camera, working out the concept and shot list, and knowing the real cost before you commit. Why Shoot Planning Matters More in Dubai Than Almost Anywhere Else

Dubai has more filming-friendly locations than most cities its size - but also more rules around them. A stunning beachfront, hotel lobby, or mall location might need a permit, a location fee, or advance notice most people don't expect. Planning properly before a shoot day isn't just about creativity - it's what prevents a shoot from being delayed, relocated last minute, or quietly costing far more than expected.

---

Step 1: Pick the Right Location (And Know What It Needs)

The location shapes everything else about the shoot - lighting conditions, background noise, crew size, and whether a permit is required at all. Public spaces, private properties, hotels, and malls in Dubai each have different rules:

- **Private venues** (offices, studios, homes) - usually the simplest, often just requiring the owner's permission - **Public locations** (beaches, streets, parks) - frequently require a filming permit from the relevant Dubai authority - **Hotels and malls** - typically need direct approval from the property's management, sometimes with an associated fee

Confirming this before the shoot date, not on the day itself, is what keeps a production on schedule.

---

Step 2: Plan the Look and Styling

Whether it's a company spokesperson, a wedding couple, or a brand ambassador in front of the camera, how they look on screen affects the finished video as much as the footage itself. A simple styling and prep conversation before the shoot - covering wardrobe colours, contrast against the background, and grooming - avoids the common mistake of arriving on set and only then realising an outfit clashes with the location or doesn't read well on camera.

---

Step 3: Build the Concept and Shot List

This is the step people skip most often, and it's usually the one that costs the most time on the actual shoot day. A clear shot list - what needs to be captured, in what order, and why - turns a vague idea into something a crew can actually execute efficiently. Without it, shoot days run long, key shots get missed, and the edit becomes far harder to piece together into a coherent video.

---

Step 4: Know the Real Cost Before You Commit

A shoot's cost depends on far more than "how many hours" - crew size, number of locations, permit fees, styling, and post-production all factor in. Building a clear, itemised estimate before committing to anything protects your budget and avoids the common surprise of extra costs appearing after the shoot is already booked.

# What Actually Changes When Your Filmmaker Has a Degree, Not Just a Diploma

Quick Answer

Backyard Studio is built by graduate filmmakers - trained through full film degree programmes, not short diploma courses - producing video content across Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain. To be fair, a diploma or self-taught path can absolutely produce skilled, talented filmmakers - qualifications alone don't guarantee good work. What a full degree programme does reliably add is deeper training in story structure, visual language, and critical feedback culture, which tends to show up in how confidently a project is planned and shaped, not just how it's filmed.

---

Let's Be Honest About What a Qualification Actually Proves

It would be easy to write this as "degree good, diploma bad" - but that's not true, and it's not a fair thing to say. Some of the most talented filmmakers working today never finished a formal course of any kind. Passion, practice, and a genuine eye for a shot matter more than a piece of paper. So this isn't about claiming one qualification makes someone a better filmmaker than another. It's about being honest about what each type of training actually covers, so you know what to ask about when you're choosing who films your project.

---

What a Diploma Typically Covers

A diploma course is usually shorter and more technical by design - and that's not a flaw, it's the format. It tends to focus on:

- How to operate a camera and basic lighting setup - Fundamentals of editing software - Practical, on-the-job style skills to get someone shooting quickly

This produces people who can competently run a shoot and deliver a video. For many projects, that's genuinely enough.

---

What a Full Film Degree Typically Adds

A degree programme is usually built over several years, and covers a wider foundation before it ever gets to "which button does what":

- **Story structure and narrative theory** - understanding why a story works, not just how to point a camera at it - **Visual language and film history** - studying how decades of filmmakers have used framing, movement, and colour to create meaning, not just aesthetics - **Critique culture** - years of having work reviewed and challenged by tutors and peers, which builds the habit of questioning your own first idea instead of settling for it - **Cross-discipline exposure** - most degree programmes require students to try directing, editing, cinematography, and sound at some point, giving graduates a genuine understanding of every role on set, not just their own - **A larger volume of practice projects** - several years of coursework typically means dozens of full projects completed and critiqued before ever working professionally

---

Where This Actually Shows Up in the Final Video

The difference isn't usually visible in "can they operate the camera" - most trained people can. It tends to show up earlier and later in the process:

- **At the planning stage** - a stronger instinct for why a shot serves the story, not just whether it looks nice - **On set** - a broader understanding of what the editor and colourist will need later, because the filmmaker has stood in those roles themselves - **In the edit** - a habit of questioning the first cut rather than accepting it, built from years of formal critique - **In problem-solving** - when something doesn't work on the day, a wider creative toolkit to solve it rather than reshooting the same idea

---

What This Means for Your Project, Practically

This isn't a reason to distrust every diploma-trained filmmaker - plenty do excellent work. It is a reasonable thing to ask about directly when comparing options, the same way you'd ask about a portfolio or process:

1. Ask what training or background the person filming and editing your project actually has 2. Ask to see a project they directed or story-shaped themselves, not just filmed 3. Ask how they approach the planning stage - do they talk about story and purpose, or only equipment and schedule? 4. Judge the portfolio itself above all - training explains tendencies, but the actual work is still the proof

---

Backyard Studio provides a written, itemised proposal for every project, regardless of scope, so pricing and deliverables are confirmed in advance.

---

How the Backyard Studio Team Approaches a Project

1. **Discovery call** - understand the actual goal behind the video, not just the format requested 2. **Story-first planning** - shot lists and locations are built around narrative purpose, not just visual preference 3. **Filming day** - a crew that understands how each role connects to the next, from camera to eventual edit 4. **Editing with critique built in** - the first cut is questioned and refined, not simply delivered as final 5. **Final delivery** - a video shaped by trained judgement at every stage, not just technical execution

---

Working With Graduate Filmmakers Across the UAE

Backyard Studio's graduate filmmaking team works across Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain, bringing the same story-first, critique-trained approach to every project regardless of location or scale.

---

Why This Matters When Choosing Backyard Studio

- **Formal film degree training** - years of study in story structure, visual language, and cross-discipline filmmaking, not a short technical course - **A team that has stood in every role** - directing, editing, cinematography, and sound, giving genuine understanding of how each part of a project connects - **Built-in critique habit** - the first idea is questioned and refined, not simply accepted and delivered - **Judged on the work itself** - a portfolio that reflects this training in practice, available to review before you book

---

Frequently Asked Questions

### Does a film degree actually make someone a better filmmaker than a diploma holder?

Not automatically - talent, experience, and practice matter more than any single qualification, and many diploma-trained or self-taught filmmakers produce excellent work. A full degree programme does typically add deeper training in story structure, visual language, and critique culture, which tends to influence how confidently a project is planned and shaped.

### What should I actually look for when comparing filmmakers, degree or not?

The strongest signal is the portfolio itself - ask to see work the person directed or shaped creatively, not just filmed, and ask how they approach the planning stage before assuming training level alone tells you everything.

### What does Backyard Studio's team background actually include?

Backyard Studio is built by graduate filmmakers trained through full film degree programmes, with cross-discipline experience across directing, cinematography, editing, and sound design.

### Does more formal training mean a higher price?

Not necessarily on its own - Backyard Studio's pricing is based on project scope, crew size, and complexity, confirmed through a written itemised proposal, rather than training background alone.

### Can a diploma-trained filmmaker still do excellent work?

Yes, absolutely - qualifications are one factor among many, and skill, experience, and a strong portfolio matter more than the specific type of training completed.

### How does story-first planning actually change the final video?

Planning shots around narrative purpose, rather than visual preference alone, tends to result in a video that holds together as a coherent story rather than a series of nice-looking but disconnected shots.

### Can I see examples of Backyard Studio's directed work, not just filmed projects?

Yes, the Backyard Studio portfolio includes projects the team has directed and creatively shaped from concept through to final edit, available to review during the consultation stage.

The Video That Never Gets Made

Here's a pattern almost every small business owner in the UAE has lived through: you decide it's time to start posting real video content. You have an idea. Then you second-guess it. Then you wait for a better idea. Then a busier week happens. Then the "perfect" concept still hasn't shown up, and three months later, the business has posted nothing at all - while a competitor with a far simpler idea has been quietly posting every week and slowly building an audience that trusts them.

This isn't a lack of good ideas. It's the trap of treating the first video like it needs to be the only video that matters. It doesn't. It just needs to exist, and be followed by another one.

---

Why Consistency Beats Perfection (And It's Not Even Close)

Social platforms reward accounts that show up regularly, not accounts that occasionally post something flawless. A business posting simple, honest content every week builds familiarity - and familiarity is what actually turns a stranger scrolling past into someone who books a call or walks into your shop. A single beautifully produced video, posted once and then followed by silence, doesn't build that same trust. It just proves you can make one good video, then disappear.

The businesses that win on social media in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and across the UAE aren't necessarily the ones with the biggest production budget. They're the ones who treated video like a habit, not an event.

# "But That Studio Quoted Me Less": Why Cheaper Isn't the Same as Better

---

Every Production House Hears This Sentence Eventually

"Another studio quoted me half the price." It's almost never said to be difficult - most clients genuinely don't know why the numbers are so different, and that's a fair question to ask. The honest answer isn't "they're worse" or "we're better." It's that you're usually comparing two completely different things and calling them the same thing.

A cheap quote is often one person: someone who shoots the video, edits it themselves, and hands it back. A production house quote is a team: a director shaping the story, a cinematographer who knows how to light and frame a shot, an editor who understands pacing, a colourist who makes it look expensive, and a sound designer who makes sure it doesn't fall flat the moment someone turns their volume up. Same brief. Very different number of hands on it.

---

What You're Actually Paying For (It's Not the Camera)

Anyone can buy a good camera. What's harder to buy is a group of people who've spent years getting good at one specific part of the process, and who know how to work together without stepping on each other's ideas.

- **A director** who takes a vague idea ("something that feels premium") and turns it into an actual plan - **A cinematographer** who knows exactly how to light a shot so it looks like a brand film, not a phone video - **An editor** who understands rhythm - when to cut, when to hold, when silence works better than music - **A colourist** who can make the same footage look flat or look cinematic, depending on skill - **A sound designer** who fixes the thing most people don't even realise is wrong until it's fixed

One freelancer can be good at one or two of these. Rarely all five. When they try to do all five themselves, something usually gets rushed - and it's almost always the part the client notices least during filming, but most once the video is finished.

---

Why "Mix and Match" Beats "One Person, Every Role"

Here's the part that's easy to miss: creative ideas get better when more than one skilled person is looking at them. A director might frame a shot one way. A cinematographer might suggest lighting it differently to make the same shot feel more premium. An editor might realise, in the cutting room, that a completely different structure tells the story better than the one that was planned. That back-and-forth - different specialists pushing the same idea further - is exactly what a solo freelancer can't fully replicate, no matter how talented they are. It's not a knock on freelancers. It's just what happens when five specialists work on one idea instead of one person wearing five hats.

---

- **Reshoots** - if one person misses a shot or a technical issue, there's no second set of eyes to catch it on the day - **Slower turnaround** - one person doing everything means everything happens in sequence, not in parallel - **Inconsistent quality** - a solo operator's skills are rarely equally strong across shooting, editing, colour, and sound - **Hidden add-ons** - a cheap quote sometimes doesn't include colour grading, sound design, or revisions, which get added as "extra" once you're already committed

The Mistake Almost Everyone Makes When Budgeting a Video Shoot

Most people planning their first video shoot cut the budget in the wrong place. They'll pay for a full-day shoot with a large crew, then skip proper audio equipment or editing time to "save money" — and the final video looks and sounds noticeably worse for it. The truth is the opposite: viewers forgive simple visuals far more than they forgive bad audio or a sloppy edit. If your budget is tight, that's exactly where to protect spending, not cut it.

- **Audio quality** — poor sound is the fastest way to make a video look unprofessional, regardless of how good the visuals are - **Editing time** — a rushed edit shows; pacing, colour grading, and sound design are where a video goes from "raw footage" to "finished product" - **Pre-production planning** — a clear script or shot list prevents wasted shoot time, which often costs more than the planning itself would have - **Experienced crew** — one skilled camera operator consistently outperforms two inexperienced ones

---

What's Actually Flexible (Cut Here If You Need To)

- **Number of locations** — one well-planned location often works better than three rushed ones - **Shoot length** — a tightly planned half-day shoot can capture what an unplanned full day would - **Crew size** — a smaller, experienced crew can deliver the same result as a larger one on simpler projects - **Extra formats** — additional social cuts can often be added later once the main video proves useful, rather than all being produced upfront

What Is Corporate Videography?

Corporate videography is the professional production of video content for business purposes — including brand films, direct video commercials (DVCs), executive interview series, internal communications, product launch videos, conference coverage, and investor presentation footage. What Is Social Media Video Production?

Social media video production is the planned, professionally executed creation of short-form and long-form video content for distribution on social media platforms — primarily Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, and Snapchat. Unlike a corporate film or broadcast commercial, social media video is produced with platform-specific formats, pacing, hook structures, and aesthetic choices that determine whether the content performs organically or disappears.

In the UAE, where social media penetration is among the highest globally (over 99% internet penetration, with Instagram and TikTok particularly dominant), professional social video has become a core component of how brands acquire customers, attract talent, and communicate credibility. TikTok: 15 second to 3 minute videos with high-energy pacing, trending audio, and natural creator-style presentation. LinkedIn: 1–3 minute professional videos — executive commentary, thought leadership, product demonstrations, case study walk-throughs. Product Video Production UAE — Pricing, Process & Guide 2026

Quick Answer

Product video production in the UAE costs between AED 5,000 and AED 25,000 for most commercial product video projects, depending on the product type, number of videos required, shooting environment (studio or location), motion graphics complexity, and post-production turnaround. Backyard Studio provides product video production across all seven UAE emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain — covering eCommerce product videos, product launch films, product demo videos, social media product content, and brand hero films for physical and digital products. Written proposals with locked pricing are confirmed before any production begins.

---

What Is Product Video Production?

Product video production is the professional filming and post-production of video content designed to demonstrate, showcase, or sell a physical or digital product. The format varies widely depending on the product category, distribution platform, and intended audience — from a 15-second Instagram Reel showing a skincare product in use, to a 3-minute cinematic launch film for a luxury watch, to a 60-second product demo video explaining how a B2B software platform works.

In the UAE, product video has become essential for brands competing on eCommerce platforms (Amazon UAE, Noon), social media shops (Instagram, TikTok Shop), and brand website product pages. UAE consumers, particularly in the Dubai market, have among the highest e-commerce spending rates in the Middle East, and video has consistently been shown to increase product page conversion rates significantly compared to photography-only listings.

Backyard Studio produces product video content for businesses across the UAE across categories including FMCG, beauty and skincare, electronics and tech, luxury goods, fashion and apparel, food and beverage, and industrial and B2B products.

---

Product Video Production Pricing in the UAE (2026)

| Package | Price (AED) | What's Included | |---|---|---| | Product Shoots (starting price) | from 1,800 | Studio product shoot, professional lighting, edited selects, multiple angles | | Social Media Product Pack | from 2,500/shoot day | Reels-format product videos, lifestyle context, all social aspect ratios, 48-hour delivery | | eCommerce Product Video (Amazon/Noon) | from 3,500 | 30–60 sec product demo, Amazon/Noon technical specs, white background + lifestyle cut | | Product Demo / Explainer Video | from 5,000 | Scripted product function demonstration, presenter or voice-over, branded motion graphics | | Product Launch Film | from 15,000 | Cinematic 2–3 min launch video, professional talent, licensed music, multi-format delivery | | DVC / Commercial for Products | 15,000 – 45,000 | Full production commercial, concept + script, casting, broadcast and digital delivery |

Factors that affect your final quote: - Product type and complexity (liquid products, electronics, luxury goods each require different studio setups) - Number of SKUs or product variants to be filmed - Shoot environment — controlled studio setup vs. lifestyle location shoot - Motion graphics and 3D animation integration - Talent requirements (product demonstrator, lifestyle model, hands-only styling) - Number of deliverable formats and platforms - Turnaround speed required

---

What's Included in Product Video Production

Pre-production: - Product brief call covering target audience, platform distribution, and conversion objective - Shot list development — product angles, usage demonstrations, lifestyle moments - Studio setup plan or location scouting - Prop and styling coordination - Written proposal with locked deliverables and pricing

Production: - Controlled studio lighting setup optimised for product category (diffused for beauty/skincare, hard light for metals and electronics) - Specialist product styling (surface, background, and prop selection) - Lifestyle or model talent when applicable - Multiple camera setups covering macro detail, product-in-use, and beauty shots

Post-production: - Edit with branded colour grade - Motion graphics — product name typography, features callouts, brand end card - Professional audio mix and licensed music - Format delivery: horizontal (16:9) for website and YouTube; vertical (9:16) for Reels, TikTok, and eCommerce mobile; square (1:1) for feed posts - Amazon and Noon technical specs compliance where applicable

---

Types of Product Videos Backyard Studio Produces

eCommerce product videos: 30–60 second videos designed for Amazon UAE, Noon, and brand DTC website product pages. These follow the functional-then-lifestyle structure: product on white or clean background, then in-use lifestyle context. The format is driven by platform technical requirements (Amazon recommends MP4, H.264, 1920×1080, minimum 30fps) and by the conversion data showing that product video increases purchase intent on UAE eCommerce platforms.

Social media product videos: Short-form vertical videos (9:16, 15–60 seconds) for Instagram Reels and TikTok, designed to drive product awareness and direct-to-consumer sales. Hook-driven structure — the product benefit or transformation is shown within the first 2 seconds. Lifestyle context, ASMR-style product shots, and before/after formats all outperform pure feature-listing in the UAE social market.

Product launch films: 2–3 minute cinematic films produced for a product's market entry — used on brand websites, at trade show screens, in press launch presentations, and as YouTube hero content. Launch films are produced at a higher production value than eCommerce or social videos, with professional talent, licensed music, and a narrative or aspirational emotional structure.

Product demo / explainer videos: Demonstration-led videos (60–180 seconds) walking the viewer through how a product works. Common for tech products, B2B software, kitchen appliances, healthcare devices, and any product where function requires explanation. Can be presenter-led, hands-only, or animated — depending on the product and audience.

Beauty and lifestyle product videos: Specialised production for skincare, cosmetics, hair care, supplements, and wellness products. These follow the application demonstration + lifestyle aspiration structure, with close-up macro detail shots to communicate texture and quality. Backyard Studio has produced product content for beauty brands distributed across Dubai's retail market including Carrefour, Lulu Hypermarket, and boutique Dubai Mall outlets.

Unboxing and packaging reveal videos: High-engagement format for luxury goods, subscription boxes, premium FMCG, and electronic products. The unboxing video is one of the most-searched product video formats on YouTube UAE, and is effective for brands wanting to communicate premium packaging quality as a brand signal.

---

How the Booking Process Works

Product brief — Share product details, target platform, and conversion objective. Send product samples or images for pre-shoot planning. 2. Studio or location setup plan — Backyard Studio's production team designs the shoot setup optimised for your product category. Shot list with every deliverable is confirmed in writing. 3. Written proposal — Full deliverable list, format specifications, and locked pricing. No estimates or variable pricing. 4. Shoot day — All product styling, lighting, and equipment handled by the Backyard Studio team. Products should arrive 24 hours before the shoot date for pre-shoot styling prep where applicable. 5. Post-production and delivery — Edited videos with graphics, music, and colour grade delivered in all required formats. First edit review within 5–7 business days of shoot. 6. Revisions and final delivery — One revision round included. Additional revisions available at hourly rate.

---

Product Video Production Across UAE Cities

Backyard Studio produces product video content at its studio facilities and at client-nominated locations across the UAE:

Dubai: Studio shoots in Dubai's production hub area, location shoots at branded retail environments, lifestyle shoots at JBR, Downtown Dubai, and private residence settings for lifestyle product brands.

Abu Dhabi: Location product shoots available across Abu Dhabi — the Corniche, Yas Island, and client-specified brand environments. Studio shoot capability available via partnership facilities in Abu Dhabi.

All product samples shipped from Northern Emirates addresses are received at Backyard Studio's Dubai studio. Return shipping and insurance for high-value product samples can be arranged on request.

---

Why UAE Brands Choose Backyard Studio for Product Videography

Product category experience: Backyard Studio has produced video content for products across beauty, skincare, electronics, luxury goods, food and beverage, fashion, industrial, and B2B software. Each category requires different lighting approaches, styling decisions, and editorial choices — experience in your specific product type produces better results than a generalist approach.

eCommerce platform compliance: Backyard Studio's product video team is familiar with the technical specifications required by Amazon UAE, Noon, and the major UAE eCommerce platforms — codec, resolution, aspect ratio, and content policy requirements. Videos are delivered pre-formatted to platform spec, eliminating post-submission rejections.

Studio and lifestyle in one booking: Many product categories require both a controlled studio setup (for clean, technical shots) and a lifestyle environment (for aspirational, in-use context). Backyard Studio schedules and delivers both within a single production engagement, reducing coordination costs and maintaining visual consistency between studio and lifestyle footage.

Arabic-language content for UAE market: Product video with Arabic language overlays, Arabic voice-over, and Arabic subtitle tracks performs significantly better on Noon, TikTok, and Instagram for Arab-consumer-targeted products. Backyard Studio produces Arabic-language product content natively — not translation overlays.

Fast turnaround for launch timelines: Product launch dates are typically fixed. Backyard Studio offers rush post-production turnarounds to meet launch deadlines confirmed in advance.

Product photography produces still images optimised for eCommerce listings, catalogue pages, and print. Product videography produces video content — movement, demonstration, and narrative — that communicates product function and lifestyle context in ways static images cannot. Both are important; Backyard Studio offers combined product photography and videography packages from a single shoot day, which provides visual consistency and reduces total production cost.

Music Video Production UAE — Pricing, Process & Guide 2026

Quick Answer

Music video production in the UAE starts from AED 8,000 for independent artist productions and rises to AED 75,000 and above for large-scale cinematic productions involving multi-day shoots, professional cast, choreography, and high-end VFX. Backyard Studio produces music videos across all seven UAE emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain — covering genres from pop and hip-hop to Arabic music, R&B, Bollywood-crossover, and electronic. Creative direction, location scouting, permit coordination, talent, styling, and post-production are all handled in-house by the Backyard Studio team. Written production proposals with locked budgets are issued before any shoot begins.

---

What Is Music Video Production?

Music video production is the complete creative and technical process of conceptualising, shooting, and editing a visual film to accompany a music track. From a single-location performance video to a multi-location narrative film with a cast, costumes, set design, and VFX, the scope of music video production varies enormously based on the artist's vision, the song's concept, and the intended distribution platform.

In the UAE, the music video production industry has grown significantly alongside Dubai's emergence as a hub for Arabic, South Asian, and international music artists. Artists recording in UAE studios — from independent musicians based in Dubai to major label artists using the UAE as a filming location for international releases — need production partners who understand both the creative demands of music video storytelling and the practical realities of filming across UAE locations. Backyard Studio has produced music videos at locations across all seven UAE emirates, including desert landscapes, urban environments, luxury properties, and controlled studio setups.

---

Music Video Production Pricing in the UAE (2026)

Music video budgets depend primarily on the number of shooting days, location complexity, cast size, wardrobe and art direction requirements, and post-production VFX. All Backyard Studio music video quotes are confirmed in writing before production begins.

| Package | Price (AED) | What's Included | |---|---|---| | Indie / Performance Video | 8,000 – 15,000 | 1 shoot day, single location, artist performance focus, basic styling, 3–5 min edited video, colour grade | | Narrative / Concept Video | 15,000 – 35,000 | 1–2 shoot days, concept development, 2–3 locations, supporting cast, 3–5 min narrative film | | Premium Cinematic Production | 35,000 – 75,000 | 2–3 shoot days, full creative direction, professional cast + extras, set design, choreography, advanced post + VFX | | Arabic / Regional Release | 15,000 – 40,000 | Arabic-language concept, culturally appropriate styling, UAE and regional location setups | | Digital Reels/Teaser Edit | from 2,500/shoot day | Short-form promotional cuts from music video footage for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts | | International Artist UAE Shoot | 40,000 – 100,000+ | Multi-day UAE production for visiting international artists, location permits, full crew and equipment |

Factors that affect your music video budget: - Number of shoot days and locations across the UAE - Cast: solo performance vs. supporting actors, dancers, extras - Set design, wardrobe, and styling requirements - Choreography direction - Drone footage (GCAA licensed — permit coordination included) - Special effects, colour effects, or VFX in post-production - Turnaround speed: standard 2–3 weeks post-production; rush available

---

What's Included in a Music Video Production

Pre-production: - Creative concept development based on song brief, mood, and artist references - Location scouting across UAE — desert, urban, studio, luxury villa, architectural - Full UAE location and filming permits coordinated by the production team - Casting and talent coordination (supporting actors, dancers, background cast) - Wardrobe, styling, and art direction planning - Shot list and storyboard creation - Written production proposal with full budget breakdown

Production: - Director and professional camera crew - Professional lighting and grip equipment - GCAA-licensed drone unit for aerial sequences - On-set styling and wardrobe management - Hair and makeup if required - Playback setup for artist lip-sync performance takes

Post-production: - Edit assembly from performance takes and narrative footage - Colour grading — cinematic grade matched to song mood and genre - Visual effects, text animations, or transitions as required - Colour effects and creative grade (moody, desaturated, warm, etc.) - Delivery in 16:9 (YouTube/streaming), 9:16 (TikTok/Reels), and 1:1 (Instagram feed) - Lyric video version available as add-on

---

Types of Music Videos Backyard Studio Produces

Performance videos: Artist-focused videos emphasising stage presence, authenticity, and visual identity. Common for hip-hop, R&B, and singer-songwriter artists. Typically one key location with thoughtful art direction — a transformed industrial space, rooftop, or studio environment.

Narrative / concept videos: Storytelling videos where the song concept is expressed through a short film narrative running parallel or intercut with performance footage. Higher production value, requires actors and location variety. Common for pop and Arabic pop artists.

Dance / choreography videos: Videos built around choreographed movement — performed by the artist alone or with a dance ensemble. Require a production team experienced in timing edits to movement, controlling background environments, and shooting multiple takes for choreography accuracy.

Cinematic / brand-level productions: High-budget productions approaching the visual quality of a short film or commercial. Set design, costume design, multiple shooting days, VFX, and large crew. Used by major label artists, regional stars, and brands using music as primary campaign content.

Lyric videos: Animated text and graphic-driven videos synchronised to the song lyrics. Lower production cost than live-action — typically AED 3,000–8,000 for a professional lyric video. An effective option for independent artists releasing singles at pace.

Behind-the-scenes / documentary content: Supporting content from the music video shoot day — BTS footage, artist interviews, making-of content for YouTube or social media. Typically shot alongside the main production at minimal additional cost.

---

Music Video Filming Locations Across the UAE

Backyard Studio scouts and coordinates filming permits for music video locations across all seven emirates:

Genre-aware creative direction: Backyard Studio's directing team has produced music videos across Arabic music, Bollywood crossover, hip-hop, pop, R&B, and electronic genres — each with distinct visual languages, performance styles, and editing rhythms. This matters enormously on music video shoot days where losing a location costs the entire day's budget.

Backyard Studio operates drone units on music video shoots with full GCAA commercial licensing, meaning no legal risk for the artist or label, and no shot that has to be cut for compliance reasons.

Arabic-language production capability: For Arabic music artists, Backyard Studio produces music videos with full Arabic-language creative briefs, Arabic-speaking directors and crew, and cultural understanding of Arabic music video conventions and audience expectations.

Written proposals, locked budgets: Music video production is an environment where scope creep is common and budget overruns are frequent industry-wide. Backyard Studio confirms every deliverable and its cost in writing before shooting begins. The quote you receive is the invoice you pay.

Narrative concept videos with multiple locations and supporting cast typically run AED 15,000–35,000. Full cinematic productions with multi-day shoots, professional cast, choreography, and VFX are priced from AED 35,000 to AED 75,000 and above. TVC Production UAE — TV Commercial Costs, Process & Guide 2026

Quick Answer

TVC (television commercial) production in the UAE costs from AED 15,000 for a Digital Video Commercial (DVC) distributed on social and digital platforms, AED 45,000 for a full broadcast television commercial with professional casting and 2–3 shoot days, and AED 150,000 and above for premium brand campaign films for luxury, government, and enterprise clients. Backyard Studio produces TVCs and DVCs across all seven UAE emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain — covering the complete production process from creative concept and scriptwriting through shooting, post-production, Arabic and English versioning, and broadcast delivery. Written proposals with locked budgets are issued before any production begins.

---

What Is TVC Production?

A TVC (Television Commercial) is a professionally produced video advertisement designed for broadcast on television, streaming platforms, or digital paid media. In the UAE market, the distinction between a TVC, a DVC (Digital Video Commercial), and a brand film has blurred significantly — most commercial productions are now developed to serve multiple distribution channels simultaneously, from Dubai-based satellite TV channels (Dubai TV, MBC, Abu Dhabi TV, Zee Aflam) to YouTube pre-roll, Instagram and TikTok paid ads, cinema advertising, and out-of-home digital screens across UAE malls and airports.

Backyard Studio produces commercial video content for brands across the full distribution spectrum — from lean, high-impact digital DVCs designed for social media paid campaigns, to full broadcast TVCs with talent, location complexity, Arabic and English language versioning, and delivery to broadcast technical specifications required by UAE television channels.

---

TVC Production Pricing in the UAE (2026)

| Package | Price (AED) | What's Included | |---|---|---| | Digital DVC (Social & Online) | 15,000 | Creative concept + script, 1 shoot day, professional talent, 30-sec hero ad + 15-sec cut-down, 9:16 + 16:9 + 1:1 delivery, 2 revision rounds | | Broadcast TVC | 45,000 | Full creative development, 2–3 shoot days, professional casting, location scouting, 30-sec TVC + cuts, Arabic + English versions, broadcast spec delivery, 3 revision rounds | | Premium Brand Campaign Film | 150,000+ | Multi-day UAE-wide production, full art direction, large cast + crew, VFX + motion graphics, original music composition, international broadcast and digital delivery | | Ad Campaign Pack (3 ads) | 35,000 – 65,000 | 3 x 30-sec or 15-sec ads sharing one shoot day, consistent creative direction, multi-format delivery across all platforms | | Corporate TVC | 25,000 – 45,000 | Business-focused commercial for B2B products/services, professional presenters, scripted narrative, broadcast and digital delivery |

Key cost drivers for UAE TVC production: - Number of shoot days (1 day vs. 2–3 days changes the budget significantly) - Talent: internal spokespeople vs. professional actors from a casting agency - Location: single controlled location vs. multi-location UAE-wide shoot - Arabic language version: voiceover only (+AED 2,000–5,000) vs. full re-shoot with Arabic-speaking talent - VFX, animation, or motion graphics complexity - Music: library track (included) vs. original composition (+AED 5,000–20,000) - Broadcast delivery specifications (prores, broadcast-grade colour grading, audio loudness specs)

---

The UAE TVC Production Process

1. Brief and creative development The process begins with a full creative brief — your brand, target audience, message, tone, and mandatory content elements. Backyard Studio's creative team develops 2–3 concept directions with treatment documents outlining the visual approach, casting direction, and location strategy. The selected concept is developed into a full script and shot list.

2. Pre-production Pre-production covers everything that happens before cameras roll: casting (from agency rosters or internal talent), location scouting and permit coordination across the UAE, wardrobe and prop sourcing, set design where required, and logistics planning. UAE commercial shoots at key locations — Dubai Marina, DWTC, Abu Dhabi Corniche — require filming permits from the Dubai Film and TV Commission or Abu Dhabi Film Commission. Backyard Studio manages all permit applications as part of the standard production process.

3. Shoot day(s) A commercial-grade shoot includes a director, director of photography (DoP), camera crew, lighting and grip team, production assistant, and on-set post coordinator. Professional actors work from call sheets with scene-by-scene schedules. Backyard Studio operates GCAA-licensed drone units on set for aerial sequences included in the creative concept.

4. Post-production Post-production for a UAE TVC includes edit assembly, colour grading to broadcast standards, professional audio mix with music and sound design, motion graphics or lower third titles, Arabic and English subtitle/caption files, and final delivery in all required technical specifications. Two to three rounds of edit review are included depending on the package.

5. Broadcast delivery For UAE television broadcast, final files are delivered to the specifications required by each channel — typically ProRes 422 or H.264 at broadcast loudness standards (-23 LUFS for international broadcast, -14 for digital platforms). Backyard Studio is familiar with the technical requirements of Dubai TV, MBC, Abu Dhabi TV, and UAE digital OOH network specifications.

---

Types of Commercial Productions Backyard Studio Creates

Brand commercials: 30–60 second brand films telling a company's story or communicating a brand positioning. Used on television, YouTube, and in pre-roll advertising campaigns.

Product launch commercials: Purpose-built ads introducing a new product to the UAE market. Typically run across broadcast, digital, and paid social simultaneously on launch day.

Promotional / offer commercials: Short-form (10–15 second) ads communicating a specific promotional offer — Ramadan campaigns, National Day offers, product discounts. Produced quickly and efficiently for seasonal campaign calendars.

Government and institutional TVCs: Commercially produced public awareness campaigns, ministerial messaging videos, and government initiative films. Backyard Studio is experienced in the protocols, approval processes, and message sensitivities required for government-commissioned commercial content.

Arabic and English bilingual campaigns: Full creative and production delivery in both Arabic and English — different scripts, different talent, different cultural nuances — produced as two complete versions that share the same core creative direction. Essential for brands targeting both UAE national audiences and expatriate consumers simultaneously.

Automotive commercial shoots: High-end car commercial production — a specialist category requiring precision driving coordination, specialised mount equipment, and the ability to shoot in UAE desert, mountain, and urban environments in a single production. Car commercial production starts from AED 25,000.

Digital commercials (DVCs): Optimised for paid social and YouTube — shorter, hook-first formats (6-second pre-rolls, 15-second skippable ads, 30-second brand films). Produced to platform best practices for paid media performance, not broadcast conventions.

---

TVC Production Across UAE Emirates

Backyard Studio manages commercial shoots across all seven UAE emirates with full permit coordination:

Dubai: All Dubai filming permits coordinated via Dubai Film and TV Commission. Key commercial locations — Downtown Dubai, Dubai Marina, JBR, DWTC, DIFC, luxury hotels, shopping malls, and desert locations south of the city.

Abu Dhabi: Abu Dhabi commercial shoots coordinated via Abu Dhabi Film Commission (twofour54). Key locations: Corniche, Yas Island, ADNEC, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque area (strict permit process), Louvre Abu Dhabi environs.

Sharjah: Expo Centre Sharjah, Sharjah arts district, industrial locations, and heritage areas. Sharjah has specific content guidelines for commercial shoots — Backyard Studio manages compliance as part of the production process.

Northern Emirates (RAK, Fujairah, Ajman, UAQ): Desert locations in RAK and Al Ain direction, mountain roads in the Hajar range, east coast beaches in Fujairah — all available for commercial shoots with appropriate permits. Northern Emirates locations are frequently used for automotive, travel, and lifestyle commercial productions.

---

Why UAE Brands Choose Backyard Studio for TVC Production

Arabic and English bilingual capability: Backyard Studio produces Arabic and English versions of commercial content with native Arabic-speaking directors, crew, and talent — not translated scripts overlaid with subtitles. This distinction matters for brands wanting commercial messaging to land authentically with UAE national and Arab expat audiences.

Full permit management: Commercial shoots across the UAE require filming permits from multiple authorities — Dubai Film and TV Commission, Abu Dhabi Film Commission, individual mall or venue permits, GCAA drone permits, and road closure permits for automotive shots. Backyard Studio manages the entire permit process, preventing the shoot-day disruptions that derail productions managed by less experienced production companies.

DVC pricing transparency: Most UAE production companies provide TVC quotes that balloon from initial estimate to final invoice. Backyard Studio provides itemised written proposals before production begins — talent, crew, locations, post-production, and delivery are all line-itemed. The proposal price is the invoice price.

GCAA-licensed drone operations: Aerial commercial sequences — product reveals from above, location establishment shots, automotive drone chases — are handled with full GCAA licensing. No unlicensed drone use that creates post-production risk or legal exposure for your brand.

How much does a TVC cost in the UAE?

TVC production in the UAE is priced by format and scope. A Digital Video Commercial (DVC) distributed on social and digital platforms starts from AED 15,000, including concept, a 1-day shoot with professional talent, 30-second and 15-second edits, and multi-format delivery. A full broadcast TVC with 2–3 shoot days, professional casting, and Arabic + English versions is AED 45,000. Premium brand campaign films for luxury and enterprise clients start from AED 150,000.

What is the difference between a TVC and a DVC in the UAE?

A TVC (Television Commercial) is produced to broadcast technical standards — specific codec, resolution, aspect ratio, and audio loudness specifications required by UAE television channels. A DVC (Digital Video Commercial) is optimised for digital distribution — social media paid ads, YouTube pre-roll, and digital screens — without the broadcast delivery requirements. Many UAE productions now produce both formats simultaneously, with broadcast and digital versions delivered from the same shoot. In budget terms, a DVC starts from AED 15,000 while a broadcast TVC starts from AED 45,000 due to the additional shooting days, crew requirements, and technical delivery standards.

Documentary Production UAE — Pricing, Process & Guide 2026

Quick Answer

Documentary production in the UAE starts from AED 25,000 for a corporate or brand documentary (15–30 minutes, 2–3 shoot days) and rises to AED 150,000 and above for full-length broadcast-quality documentaries with extensive fieldwork, multiple interview subjects, archival research, and multi-platform delivery. Written production proposals with locked budgets are confirmed before production begins.

---

What Is Documentary Production?

A documentary film is a non-fiction video production that uses real people, real events, and real environments to tell a story — as opposed to scripted fiction. In a business and brand context, documentary production covers a wide range of formats: a 10-minute company origin story for a website; a 30-minute profile of a founder's journey from idea to IPO; a social impact film documenting a government initiative; a biographical film about a sports personality, entrepreneur, or cultural figure; or a full-length feature documentary for festival submission or streaming platform release.

In the UAE, documentary production has grown significantly as brands, government entities, and individuals recognise the power of authentic storytelling to build credibility, communicate values, and achieve reach on digital platforms. A well-produced documentary generates trust signals that no advertising campaign can replicate — because it shows rather than claims. Backyard Studio has produced documentary content for corporations, government departments, individual entrepreneurs, athletes, and cultural institutions across the UAE.

---

Documentary Production Pricing in the UAE (2026)

| Format | Price (AED) | What's Included | |---|---|---| | Corporate / Brand Documentary (10–20 min) | 25,000 – 50,000 | 2–3 shoot days, 3–6 interview subjects, b-roll across UAE locations, narration, full edit + colour grade | | Success Story / Journey Film (5–15 min) | 15,000 – 30,000 | 1–2 shoot days, individual or team focus, interview + observational footage, cinematic edit | | Biographical Film (individual profile) | 30,000 – 70,000 | Full individual profile — interviews, archival stills/footage, location recreation, 20–45 min deliverable | | Social Impact Documentary | 35,000 – 80,000 | Multi-shoot fieldwork, multiple community subjects, voiceover narrative, subtitles, broadcast/streaming delivery | | Full-Length Documentary (45–90 min) | 80,000 – 200,000+ | Extended research + pre-production, multiple shoot days, archival research, professional narrator, broadcast delivery | | Mini-Documentary / Brand Origin Film (3–8 min) | 12,000 – 25,000 | Compact cinematic short, 1 shoot day, 1–3 subjects, professional edit — ideal for website, social, and investor decks |

Factors that affect documentary production costs: - Duration of the finished film (10 minutes vs. 45 minutes = very different edit complexity) - Number of interview subjects and their geographic locations across the UAE - B-roll complexity: talking head interviews only vs. observational fieldwork + location coverage - Archival research and integration of historical materials (photos, footage, documents) - Narration or voice-over recording - Animation, infographics, or motion graphics for data or historical sequences - Subtitles and language versions (Arabic, English) - Distribution platform: internal use vs. broadcast submission vs. international festival delivery

---

Types of Documentaries Backyard Studio Produces

Corporate and brand documentaries: A 15–30 minute film telling the story of a company — its founding, its people, its values, and its impact. Used on corporate websites, investor pitch decks, internal all-hands meetings, and as foundational brand content. Particularly effective for companies with a compelling origin story, a family legacy, or a clear social mission.

Success story films: A focused film profile — typically 5–15 minutes — documenting an individual's or organisation's achievement. Common for entrepreneurs, athletes, executives, and organisations commemorating milestones. Combines a structured interview with observational footage of the subject in their working environment, complemented by locations that contextualise the story.

Journey films: A film documenting the process of building something over time — a startup's road to funding, an athlete's training journey to a major competition, a creative project from concept to completion. Journey films work particularly well as serialised YouTube content (episodic) or as a single-long-form documentary capping a defined period.

Biographical films: A film profile of an individual — a business leader, creative figure, athlete, scholar, or cultural personality. More extensive than a success story film, biographical productions require deeper research, multiple interview subjects (colleagues, family, collaborators), archival materials, and a longer production timeline. Backyard Studio has produced biographical films for UAE-based entrepreneurs and sports personalities.

Social impact documentaries: Films documenting the work of NGOs, government initiatives, humanitarian programmes, or community organisations. These are typically produced for donor reporting, government submissions, international conference screenings, or public awareness campaigns. Backyard Studio produces social impact documentaries in Arabic and English, and is experienced working within the sensitivity requirements of UAE government and humanitarian organisations.

Individual video portfolio / achievement profile: A short documentary profile (3–8 minutes) designed to document an individual's career achievements, skills, or story — used by professionals, athletes, artists, and academics as a high-credibility digital portfolio piece. Increasingly used on LinkedIn, personal websites, and speaker bureau profiles.

---

How the Documentary Production Process Works

1. Research and development Documentary production begins with a research phase: reviewing existing materials (articles, photos, videos, reports), conducting preliminary interviews with the subject(s), and identifying the key story arc and structural approach. Backyard Studio's development process produces a treatment document — a written outline of the film's narrative structure, interview subjects, key locations, and visual approach — before any filming begins.

2. Pre-production Pre-production covers interview scheduling and location confirmation, release forms and clearance for archive materials, permit applications for UAE filming locations, and equipment planning. For documentaries involving government officials, royalty adjacent subjects, or restricted access locations, Backyard Studio manages the coordination and clearance process.

3. Principal photography Documentary shoots are typically non-scripted but structured: interview sessions with key subjects using a pre-agreed question framework, observational (fly-on-the-wall) footage in the subject's working environment, location b-roll across UAE settings relevant to the story, and any reconstruction or illustrative footage the narrative requires.

4. Post-production Documentary post-production is the most time-intensive phase: assembling interview footage into a coherent narrative structure, selecting and integrating b-roll, creating motion graphic sequences for data or historical context, recording narration or voice-over, music supervision and licensing, colour grading, audio mix, and subtitling. A 20-minute corporate documentary typically requires 3–4 weeks of post-production.

5. Delivery Delivery formats depend on distribution: H.264 MP4 for web/streaming (website, YouTube, Vimeo); ProRes for broadcast submission; DCP for cinema screening; and multi-format social cuts (Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) from key documentary sequences for promotional distribution.

---

Documentary Filming Across UAE Emirates

Backyard Studio conducts documentary fieldwork across all seven UAE emirates:

Dubai: Corporate headquarters in DIFC, Business Bay, and Dubai Media City; entrepreneurial environments in Dubai Internet City and Al Quoz creative district; government facility filming with appropriate clearances; iconic Dubai locations providing visual context for the UAE's contemporary story.

Abu Dhabi: Government and institutional documentary subjects — ministries, cultural institutions, and sovereign wealth-adjacent organisations — are predominantly Abu Dhabi-based. Backyard Studio is experienced in the protocols, clearance requirements, and production sensitivities of Abu Dhabi government filming.

Sharjah: Cultural and heritage documentary subjects — Sharjah's museums, cultural districts, and heritage areas. Also industrial and manufacturing documentary subjects at Sharjah's industrial zones.

Northern Emirates: Ras Al Khaimah's Jebel Jais, mountain communities, and heritage villages; Fujairah's east coast port and fishing communities; Ajman and Umm Al Quwain's traditional boat-building and coastal heritage sites — all compelling locations for documentaries exploring UAE identity, geography, and heritage beyond the Dubai narrative.

---

Why Organisations Choose Backyard Studio for Documentaries

Long-form storytelling experience: Producing a compelling 20-minute documentary is fundamentally different from producing a 30-second ad. The structural decisions — what to show first, how to build tension, how to pace an interview sequence, when to use silence — require a different creative discipline. Backyard Studio's directing team has structured and delivered long-form documentary content across corporate, biographical, and social impact categories.

Arabic-language documentary capability: UAE stories exist in Arabic and English, and many of the most compelling subjects — government officials, UAE national entrepreneurs, cultural figures, and heritage communities — tell their stories most authentically in Arabic. Backyard Studio conducts and directs documentary interviews in Arabic with native-speaking directors, without translation layers that reduce the authenticity of the subject's voice.

Sensitive subject handling: Documentaries in the UAE often involve individuals and institutions that require careful handling — government officials, business leaders, royal family-adjacent organisations, and culturally sensitive community subjects. Backyard Studio's production team understands the cultural, legal, and diplomatic considerations of documentary production in the UAE environment.

Multi-platform distribution strategy: Backyard Studio delivers documentary content in formats optimised for every intended distribution point — website, YouTube, Vimeo, broadcast submission, and festival screening — alongside short-form promotional cuts for social media. The documentary becomes a content ecosystem, not just a single film.

What Is Short Film & Web Series Production?

A web series is a scripted, episodic narrative produced for digital distribution — YouTube, Shahid, OSN, and independent streaming channels. YouTube series and show production is the professional production of episodic video content for YouTube — structured as a recurring format (a show, a series, a channel programme) rather than a one-off video. The production formats within YouTube series production are varied: a weekly talking-head interview show, a documentary-style travel or food series, a brand-funded educational series, a CEO thought-leadership show, a behind-the-scenes business series, or a podcast production filmed for video distribution. What Is Travel Videography?

Travel videography is the professional filming of destinations, experiences, and journeys — produced for tourism boards, hotels and resorts, travel brands, airlines, adventure tourism operators, lifestyle brands, and independent travel content channels. The output ranges from a 90-second Instagram Reel showcasing a resort's experience to a 10-minute YouTube travel documentary exploring Ras Al Khaimah's Hajar Mountains, to a full-length 30-minute destination film commissioned by a UAE tourism authority.

In the UAE, the travel videography market is particularly active. The country hosts over 20 million international visitors per year across all seven emirates, and the competition for travel content visibility — on YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and tourism authority digital channels — is intense. High-quality travel videography is a primary marketing investment for UAE hotels, resorts, tourism operators, and destination management companies. The UAE offers extraordinary geographic and visual variety across its seven emirates — a range that no other country of comparable size can match. Backyard Studio has produced travel content across all of these environments:

Brand Profile Revamp & Individual Video Portfolio UAE — Pricing 2026

Quick Answer

Individual video portfolio production and brand profile revamp content in the UAE starts from AED 5,000 for a professional personal brand video and rises to AED 25,000 and above for a full brand identity refresh production including hero video, social content suite, and photography. Backyard Studio creates individual video portfolios, personal brand films, executive profile videos, professional athlete profiles, and brand refresh content for individuals and businesses repositioning in the UAE market. Productions cover all seven UAE emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain. Contact Backyard Studio on +971 58 588 2685.

---

What Is a Profile Revamp & Individual Video Portfolio?

A profile revamp is a professional video production specifically designed to update, refresh, and reposition an individual's or brand's visual presence and public identity — used when a person or company has grown, changed direction, or entered a new market and needs content that reflects who they are now rather than who they were when their existing content was produced.

An individual video portfolio is a curated collection of professionally produced video content documenting an individual's skills, achievements, experience, and professional identity — used by athletes, performing artists, executives, academics, consultants, architects, and creative professionals to present their work credibly to employers, clients, agents, competition committees, and media.

In the UAE, where professional reputation is heavily driven by digital presence — LinkedIn, personal websites, and Google search results — a professional video portfolio or brand refresh is an investment in first impressions at scale. A polished 90-second personal brand video on LinkedIn or a well-produced portfolio page on a personal website reaches more professional opportunities than any number of written profiles.

---

Profile Revamp & Video Portfolio Pricing in the UAE (2026)

| Package | Price (AED) | What's Included | |---|---|---| | Personal Brand Video (60–90 sec) | from 5,000 | Half-day shoot, 1 location, professional lighting, edit + colour grade, social format delivery | | Executive Profile Video | from 8,000 | Interview + b-roll at workspace/location, professional lighting + audio, 2–4 min profile video | | Individual Achievement Portfolio (3–8 min) | 12,000 – 25,000 | Full individual profile — interview, location coverage, achievement showcase, documentary style | | Athlete Video Portfolio | 10,000 – 20,000 | Training footage + interview + highlight compilation, multi-location, social reel + full portfolio version | | Brand Profile Revamp (full package) | 20,000 – 45,000 | New hero video + social content suite + photography — complete visual identity refresh | | Performing Artist Portfolio | 8,000 – 18,000 | Performance footage + interview + achievement profile — music, dance, theatre, comedy |

---

What's Included in an Individual Video Portfolio Production

Pre-production: - Portfolio strategy consultation — identifying the target audience, platform, and professional objective of the portfolio - Shot list based on skills, achievements, and environments to showcase - Location selection — office, training facility, studio, outdoor, or combination - Styling and wardrobe guidance - Interview question framework based on the individual's story and objectives

Production: - Professional camera crew with cinema-grade camera - Professional three-point lighting setup - Lapel microphone and directional audio - B-roll: workplace, training, skills in action, location context - Interview — structured and conversational, with multiple takes for natural delivery

Post-production: - Full portfolio video edit (2–8 minutes) - Short-form social version (60–90 seconds for LinkedIn and Instagram) - Colour grade - Branded lower thirds with name, title, and credentials - Music bed (licensed) - Subtitle file (English and/or Arabic) - Multi-format delivery: 16:9 (website/YouTube), 9:16 (social), 1:1 (LinkedIn)

---

Types of Profile & Portfolio Content Backyard Studio Creates

Personal brand videos: A concise 60–90 second video that introduces an individual to their professional network — who they are, what they do, who they help, and what makes them distinctive. The most widely used format for LinkedIn profile videos, speaker bureau pages, and personal website hero content. Used by executives, consultants, coaches, entrepreneurs, and any individual whose work depends on personal credibility and relationship trust.

Executive profile videos: A more detailed (2–4 minute) profile of a senior executive — combining interview with workspace and work-in-action b-roll. Used for company "About the Team" pages, keynote speaker profiles, board appointment announcements, award nomination submissions, and business publication profiles.

Individual achievement portfolios: A documentary-style video profile (3–8 minutes) documenting an individual's career achievements — most commonly produced for senior professionals transitioning between sectors, entrepreneurs announcing a new venture, and individuals seeking board or advisory appointments. The format mirrors a documentary short: structured interview, archival stills and video where relevant, and b-roll illustrating the individual's environment and work.

Athlete video portfolios: Professional video portfolios for UAE-based and visiting athletes — combining training footage, competition highlights, coach or team testimony, and an athlete interview. Used for team selection submissions, sponsorship approaches, scholarship applications, and sports media coverage. Backyard Studio has produced athlete portfolios for football, cricket, MMA, swimming, and equestrian athletes in the UAE.

Performing artist portfolios: Video portfolios for musicians, dancers, actors, stand-up comedians, and performing artists — combining performance footage with an interview contextualising the artist's background, influences, and professional achievements. Used for agency representation applications, festival programming submissions, and entertainment industry pitch materials.

Brand profile revamps: For companies whose existing video presence no longer reflects their current size, service offering, or market positioning — a full brand profile revamp production creates a new hero video, updated social content suite, and coordinated photography in a single production engagement. Common triggers for brand revamp commissions include: major service expansion, geographic market entry, leadership change, rebranding, investment announcement, and significant company milestone.

---

Profile Revamp & Portfolio Production Across UAE Emirates

Dubai: The UAE's primary professional networking market — LinkedIn activity, personal brand visibility, and executive profile credibility are most actively relevant in Dubai's DIFC, Business Bay, and DWTC professional ecosystem. Backyard Studio's individual portfolio productions in Dubai typically use the subject's own office, an DIFC or Business Bay lobby location, or an outdoor urban setting in Downtown.

Abu Dhabi: Government officials, senior public sector executives, academics (ADNEC and UAE university connections), and senior private sector figures in Abu Dhabi commission profile and portfolio productions for international conference, award submission, and government programme contexts.

Sharjah and Northern Emirates: Entrepreneurial and cultural figures based in the Northern Emirates — artists, traditional craftspeople, regional business owners, and academic professionals — are increasingly commissioning individual video portfolios as digital presence becomes essential for professional opportunity across the UAE and Gulf region.

---

Why UAE Professionals Choose Backyard Studio for Portfolio Content

Interview direction: The most common problem with professionally filmed executive portraits and profile videos is that the subject looks and sounds uncomfortable on camera — reading from notes, speaking in corporate jargon, or visibly nervous. Backyard Studio's directors are experienced in helping interview subjects relax and speak naturally, using conversational interview techniques and multiple takes to find the authentic, credible version of the individual rather than the performed one.

Understanding of professional objectives: A profile video for a keynote speaker has different requirements from a portfolio for a professional athlete, which is different from an executive profile for a private equity investment committee. Backyard Studio develops each portfolio brief around the specific professional objective — the target audience, the decision they're being asked to make, and what they need to see and hear to make it.

Dubai LinkedIn market familiarity: The UAE's professional LinkedIn market is one of the most active and business-critical in the world. Backyard Studio understands what performs on UAE LinkedIn — the visual hooks, the length, the captioning conventions, and the storytelling approach that drives profile views, connection requests, and inbound professional enquiries.

Photography and video coordination: A brand profile revamp is most effective when photography and video are produced in a single coordinated production day — consistent styling, lighting, and location across both photo and video outputs creates a unified brand presence that individual photography or video shoots produced separately cannot match. Backyard Studio coordinates photography and video content in a single brief and shoot.

---

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a personal brand video cost in the UAE?

Personal brand video production in the UAE starts from AED 5,000 for a 60–90 second professional brand video with half-day production, one location, professional lighting and audio, edit, colour grade, and social format delivery. Executive profile videos (2–4 minutes) start from AED 8,000. A full individual achievement portfolio documentary (3–8 minutes) is priced from AED 12,000 to AED 25,000.

What is a brand profile revamp and when do I need one?

A brand profile revamp is a comprehensive update of a business's video and photography presence — new hero video, new social content suite, and updated brand photography — produced in a coordinated production to ensure visual consistency across all platforms. You likely need a brand revamp if: your existing video content is more than 2 years old, your company has significantly grown or changed services, you're entering a new market, or your leadership team has changed. Backyard Studio's brand profile revamp packages start from AED 20,000.

Can you produce an athlete video portfolio in the UAE?

Yes. Backyard Studio produces professional athlete video portfolios for UAE-based and visiting athletes across all sports — football, cricket, MMA, swimming, equestrian, golf, basketball, and others. A standard athlete portfolio production (training footage + competition highlights + interview) is priced from AED 10,000 and includes social reel cuts (60–90 seconds for Instagram) and a full portfolio version (3–5 minutes) for agency and sponsorship submissions.

Do you produce portfolio videos for performing artists?

Yes. Musicians, dancers, actors, and performing artists working in the UAE commission video portfolios for agency applications, festival submissions, and media coverage. Backyard Studio produces performing artist portfolio videos that combine performance footage (live or specially filmed) with an artist interview. Productions are priced from AED 8,000 and delivered in formats suitable for YouTube, Instagram, agent submission packages, and festival digital programmes.

How long does a personal brand video take to produce?

A personal brand video (60–90 seconds) takes 1–2 weeks from brief to delivery: pre-production consultation and shot planning (3–5 days), half-day shoot, and 3–5 days post-production. An executive profile video or full portfolio documentary takes 2–4 weeks depending on complexity and locations. Rush timelines are available for award submissions and time-sensitive professional milestones.

Can you update my brand video to reflect a new service or company direction?

Yes. Backyard Studio produces brand refresh productions for companies whose existing video content no longer accurately represents them. A targeted brand refresh — re-filming specific sections of an existing company video to reflect new services, a new team, or a new market position — is often more cost-effective than a full re-production. Backyard Studio reviews existing content before recommending a full revamp or a targeted update.

Do you produce individual video portfolios in Arabic?

Yes. Individual video portfolios and personal brand content in Arabic — for UAE national professionals presenting to Arabic-language professional networks, government bodies, or Gulf Arab business environments — are produced with Arabic-speaking directors and delivered with Arabic subtitles and captions. Arabic-language LinkedIn content for UAE national professionals significantly outperforms English-language equivalents in terms of professional network engagement.
